subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should first-party iOS Siri/App Intent execution be added, and if so should it route through paired-node identity/chat.send or node.event, or through a hardened /hooks/agent boundary?
rationale: The requested feature aligns with iOS companion-app direction, but it adds a new voice and Shortcuts agent-execution surface where auth, session routing, local confirmation, reply delivery, and operator control are product and security choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Use paired-node identity
options.body: Build the intent around the existing authenticated iOS node/operator session and chat.send or node.event semantics, with explicit local confirmation and session routing.

options.title: Limit scope to Talk Mode launch
options.body: Treat the open Action Button/Talk Mode PR as the only first-party shortcut surface and leave parameterized Siri questions out of scope for now.

options.title: Defer native Siri support
options.body: Keep Shortcuts/webhook or Talk Mode workarounds until iOS voice-entry product direction is clearer.

recommendation.title: Use paired-node identity
recommendation.body: Build the intent around the existing authenticated iOS node/operator session and chat.send or node.event semantics, with explicit local confirmation and session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history signal for iOS Gateway/session boundaries and security-sensitive iOS routing decisions.
